page.not_used_title: Not used with this model and placement
notes: Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ1_M-00001-of-00002.gguf, 48 expert layers of 256 experts, 23.42 GiB of experts; 11.07 GiB of them in host RAM (--experts-in-ram 24 (given)).
Host: 31.3 GiB RAM, 28.3 GiB available now, 26 GiB usable for the model; L3 32 MiB (sysfs index3: 32 MiB shared by cpus 0-15).

rows.name: --cache-ram
rows.reason: off when the host experts (counted twice when the build can pin them: the mmap pages the server still reads and a full pinned copy), the tables' resident rows and the default 8 GiB prompt cache exceed the 26 GiB usable RAM; the pin budget below gets that RAM

rows.name: -ub
rows.reason: the chunk BoltBeam's prompt limit picks for this machine (the offload page's prompt setup): the smallest within the policy tie of the best; host experts are uploaded once per chunk, so bigger chunks upload less (with experts in RAM, 4096 measured 15% faster than 2048)

rows.name: -b
rows.reason: raised to -ub when -ub is larger (the command does it); larger than -ub measured no effect: -b 8192 at -ub 4096, 10k, 4,295 vs 4,312 tok/s (the server's head and near-end breaks still set the decode calls)

rows.name: LLAMA_WS
rows.reason: on: it only engages for prefill chunks of at least LLAMA_WS_MIN_TOKENS tokens with experts in host RAM; decode takes the stock path (measured unchanged, 24.6 vs 24.8 tok/s)

rows.name: LLAMA_WS_MIN_TOKENS
rows.reason: left at the patch's 1024: at -ub 4096 on a 10k prompt 256 and 1024 measured the same (4,329 vs 4,312 tok/s wall; the chat head batch is shorter than either). It decides only chunks smaller than it, so it matters only with small -ub (at -ub 256 and 512 the streamed path measured 1.8-1.9x the stock one)

rows.name: LLAMA_WS_PIN_GIB
rows.reason: a pinned copy is a second copy: the server's short chunks still read every host expert from the mmap, so all 11.07 GiB stay in the page cache. Pinned + host experts + tables' resident rows (0.08 GiB) + prompt cache (0 GiB) must fit the 26 GiB usable RAM (28.3 GiB available when this ran, less the 2 GiB margin). Conservative by the margin: on the 31 GB box the rule allows 1 GiB at -cmoe where 4 GiB measured best (+5% over none) and 8 GiB collapsed. Run it with no other model server holding RAM. What it pins is whole expert tensors in load order, not experts by use: a measured routing profile (boltbeam routing MODEL --engine E; on this model the hottest 10% of experts take 47% of selections) says which experts a pin should hold first, which this patch cannot do yet, so that is advice only, not a setting

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_RING_MIB
rows.reason: a quarter of the 32 MiB L3 the copying core shares (sysfs index3: 32 MiB shared by cpus 0-15), a power of two: the memcpy's writes stay in cache and the DMA reads them from there, so staging is not DRAM-bound twice. The quarter is the measured best on one L3 size (32 MiB); other sizes are extrapolated by it

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_CHUNK_KIB
rows.reason: the ring in eight chunks, so the CPU fills one while the DMA drains the others (measured: 8 chunks beat 4 at the same ring)

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_SLOTS
rows.reason: 4 slots run ~1.3 layers ahead, enough to overlap; 8 measured slower (1,444 vs 1,485 tok/s) and cost VRAM. Streaming further ahead is not a lever: Strata's own stream-ahead off measured the same (6,039 vs 6,045 tok/s)

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_THREADS
rows.reason: the staging copy is bound by RAM, not by one core: 2 and 4 threads measured slower (880 and 305 vs 1,661 tok/s)

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_PAGEABLE
rows.reason: a debugging switch: pageable copies measured 751 vs 1,661 tok/s with the ring

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_MMID_PAR_MIN
rows.reason: the patch's crossover (outputs are bit-identical either way; at 10k it cut mm_ids 82 -> 26 ms); confirmed by --measure

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_MMQ_ID_J
rows.reason: a sweep knob, left unset: wider tiles were measured slower (J=128 at -ub 2048: expert MMQ 354 -> 395 ms); llama.cpp's mean-columns rule was already the best of the sweep

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_BATCH_GET_STAGING
rows.reason: on: each fresh 112 MiB pin cost ~40 ms per checkpoint; staging measured +4.5% at 10k, results bit-identical

rows.name: GGML_CUDA_BATCH_GET_STAGING_MAX_MIB
rows.reason: a cap on pinned memory: the largest staged span measured 448 MiB with the prompt cache on (128 MiB with --cache-ram 0), under the cap

rows.name: LLAMA_SERVER_CKPT_MIN_HEAD
rows.reason: 256 with experts in host RAM: the chat template's short head (42 tokens here) otherwise runs as its own batch, which uploads every host layer's experts per expert from pageable memory (2.6 GB, ~250 ms) and then takes a checkpoint sync; measured +16% at 10k (4,551 -> 5,278 tok/s wall) and +53% at 2.7k (3,089 -> 4,731). Outputs are not bitwise identical (the batch boundaries move): the first argmax divergences are near-ties (top-2 probabilities within 0.01-0.09), the same envelope as stock -ub 2048 vs 4096; checkpoint restore still works
